rules: Every downstream surface (site, llms.txt, every repo README, registry descriptions, model cards) copies the strings in `blocks` word for word. Do not paraphrase.
No number appears without its tokenizer and its N. Numbers come from docs/metrics-baseline.md only.
The name is `toke`, lower case, always. `Token-Optimised Language` is a descriptor, never the name.
Change this file first; downstream surfaces are then re-copied and `make check-canonical` re-run.

name.casing: lower case in every heading, sentence, description, README and registry field, including sentence-initial position
name.descriptor_rule: a descriptor only, never the name; never write "Toke" or "TOKE"

type.value: a compiled, statically typed, general-purpose programming language with an LLVM backend, designed as a code-generation target for large language models
type.not: not a DSL, not a template language, not a serialization format, not a prompt syntax

purpose_one_sentence.value: toke is a compiled programming language designed for LLM code generation: small, strictly structured, and canonical, so that generated code is cheap to constrain while it is being produced, cheap for a compiler to verify once it is, and compact in whatever unit the model generates in.

spec_version.note: v0.3 (docs/spec/toke-spec-v0.3.md) is historical and superseded; v0.4 is the authority for every fact on this page.

keywords.note: Supersedes the v0.3 "13 keywords" wording: both `mut` and `sc` are keywords, verified against the lexer keyword table. The logical operators are lexical, not keywords.

character_set.composition: 26 lowercase letters, 10 digits, 23 symbols; no uppercase, no underscores
character_set.note: Story 132.14 resolved this against `src/lexer.c`, which is the ground truth: in PROFILE_DEFAULT the lexer rejects exactly eight printable ASCII characters in structural position (' , ? [ \ ] _ `) and accepts every other symbol. The earlier counts were both wrong — the RFC's 56 omitted `%` and `&` (live operators) and called `^`/`~` reserved (story 114.8 assigned them bitwise XOR and NOT); the 55 wording omitted `^`, `~`, `%` and `&`. Reproduce with `python3 scripts/verify_project_facts.py --probe`.

grammar.value: backtrack-free with bounded lookahead of up to 3 tokens
grammar.long_form: The grammar is backtrack-free: the parser never rescans input it has already consumed. A small, enumerated set of productions (E1-E5) require bounded lookahead of up to 3 tokens, never more; an implementation that backtracks, or that requires unbounded lookahead at any production, is non-conforming.

retired_claim.claim: strict LL(1), one token of lookahead
retired_claim.why: the v0.3 claim "was not accurate for the real grammar"

grammar.mechanical_argument: A small backtrack-free grammar with bounded lookahead is still cheap to constrain during decoding and cheap to parse: the pushdown automaton behind a token mask stays small and the masks stay cheap. The argument never depended on the label.
grammar.source: docs/spec/toke-spec-v0.4.md §E; docs/spec/grammar.ebnf Appendix A (FIRST-sets and the enumerated exceptions)

canonical_form.value: one canonical form per construct, chosen by measurement in a 46-entry pattern catalogue and reproduced by `tkc --min`
canonical_form.note: 46 entries across 10 families (41 provisional, 5 blocked; 11 carry a distinct hot-path form). A form becomes canonical only by being best-or-tied on tokens and runtime, and all candidate forms must print byte-identical output.

compiler.name: tkc
compiler.value: tkc, the reference compiler: single-pass C99, zero dependencies beyond LLVM, native binaries for x86-64 and ARM64, and structured diagnostics with stable error codes, machine-parseable spans and a fix field.

tokenizer.value: No toke tokenizer currently beats a general-purpose one. The shipped 8K SentencePiece model needs 15.4% more tokens than cl100k_base on canonical v0.4 `tkc --min` text (N = 2,000 stratified corpus records, 2026-09-18); the v0.3 16,384-vocab tokenizer only appears to win (0.545x) because a null `unk_token` silently deletes every backslash. No "purpose-built tokenizer beats cl100k" claim is supportable until the v0.4 tokenizer is trained and locked against the Phase-3 anchor of cl100k_base = 242,427 tokens on that exact sample (story 116.9).

benchmark.value: toke-eval. The 60 Gate-1 JSON-CLI tasks were re-delivered on v0.4 on 2026-09-19: 60/60 `tkc --check`, 60/60 hidden tests (120 cases each), lint 0/0, and 4,787 cl100k_base tokens of `--min` text against 3,565 for equivalent Python (N = 60).
benchmark.caveat: The programs are hand-written, not model-generated (27 ids are pure `--migrate` output, 33 were hand-repaired), so the set measures what the language can express, not what a model produces. It may not be quoted as a model result or as a reduction against Python.

models.value: No v0.4-native model exists and none has been trained since April 2026. The most recent model gate is Gate 2, 2026-05-22: Qwen 2.5 Coder 7B + QLoRA on v0.3 syntax, 100% compile Pass@1 and 55.6% functional (272/489) on the curated 500-hidden + 200-eval set. The honest floor is the full-local re-audit of all 1,748 v0.3.9 corpus programs: 37.5% compile (655/1,748) and about 2.2% fully correct (38 PASS).
models.rule: Never quote the 100% without the curated set it was measured on, and never present the August 2026 corpus freeze as a model gate.

source_code.value: github.com/karwalski/toke — compiler, specification and standard library, Apache-2.0. The project is eleven public repositories under github.com/karwalski, plus two private ones; the site is tokelang.dev, built and served by ooke.

one_liner.value: toke: a compiled language designed for LLM code generation, with a small grammar, one canonical form and compiler verification.

paragraph.value: toke is a compiled programming language designed for LLM code generation. It has 14 keywords, a 59-character set, a backtrack-free grammar with bounded lookahead, and one canonical form per construct, chosen by measurement in a 46-pattern catalogue and reproduced by `tkc --min`. That makes generated code cheap to constrain during decoding, cheap for a compiler to verify afterwards, and compact to emit. Token efficiency is one measured property of toke, always reported with its tokenizer and its baseline, not the whole claim.

token_efficiency_short_form.value: **Token efficiency, measured:** under one shared tokenizer (cl100k_base) toke costs **1.34× [1.22, 1.48]** the tokens of equivalent Python on the 60 Gate-1 tasks (N = 60, 2026-09-19) — more, not fewer. The v0.3-era "52% fewer tokens" figure was a *tokenizer-vs-tokenizer* measurement on identical toke text (Toke-16K v0.3 vs cl100k_base, N = 42) and is superseded: on canonical v0.4 text the shipped 8K tokenizer needs **15.4% more** tokens than cl100k_base (N = 2,000). See `docs/metrics-baseline.md`.
token_efficiency_short_form.source: docs/metrics-baseline.md § Canonical wording for token-efficiency claims, short form (story 132.6)

disambiguation.value: toke is a programming language. It is not the slang word for a draw on a cigarette, not the cannabis brands that use the name, not the TOKE crypto tokens, not Tokelau or its `.tk` country-code domain, and not tokelang.com, which is an unrelated third-party project. The language is at tokelang.dev and github.com/karwalski/toke.

subprojects.value: ooke, loke and moke are toke sub-projects, not separate products: ooke is toke's web framework and static site generator, and it serves tokelang.dev; loke is toke's local intelligence layer; moke is loke's data-analysis demo. All three are written in toke.

LL(1).instead: backtrack-free, or backtrack-free with bounded lookahead

52% fewer tokens (unqualified).instead: the token-efficiency short form above, verbatim

42% reduction vs Python.instead: withdrawn outright; toke costs about 1.34x Python's cl100k_base tokens
